### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.ai

### Question

I've tried setting up custom tree sitter text objects like described [here](https://github.com/echasnovski/mini.nvim/blob/4e873f36552ac7c15a824f36783c629493f78d0c/doc/mini-ai.txt#L715). These seem to work fine with lua, but with every other language I have tried (javascript, cpp, bash) nvim tells me: (mini.ai) No textobject "iF" found covering region within 50 lines and 'search_method = 'cover_or_next''. Here is my config:

```
use {
    'nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter',
    lazy = false,
    build = ':TSUpdate',
    config = function()
        require('nvim-treesitter').setup({
            -- Directory to install parsers and queries to (prepended to 'runtimepath' to have priority)
            install_dir = vim.fn.stdpath('data') .. '/site'
        })
    end
}
use {
    "nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter-textobjects",
    branch = "main",
    init = function()
    -- Disable entire built-in ftplugin mappings to avoid conflicts.
    -- See https://github.com/neovim/neovim/tree/master/runtime/ftplugin for built-in ftplugins.
    vim.g.no_plugin_maps = true
    -- Or, disable per filetype (add as you like)
    -- vim.g.no_python_maps = true
    -- vim.g.no_ruby_maps = true
    -- vim.g.no_rust_maps = true
    -- vim.g.no_go_maps = true
    end,
    config = function()
    -- put your config here
    end,
}
use {
    'nvim-mini/mini.ai',
    config = function()
    local spec_treesitter = require('mini.ai').gen_spec.treesitter
        require('mini.ai').setup({
            custom_textobjects = {
                ['F'] = spec_treesitter({ a = '@function.outer', i = '@function.inner' }),
                ['c'] = spec_treesitter({ a = '@class.outer', i = '@class.inner' }),
                ['i'] = spec_treesitter({ a = '@conditional.outer', i = '@conditional.inner' }),
            },
        })
    end
}
````

I apologize in advance if the problem is super obvious, but I'm not sure what I did wrong.

comment_data.body:
Hello @KismetPartisan,

Thanks for the question!

That message can appear when the enclosing function contains a lot of lines. Default `MiniAi.config.n_lines` is 50. Does it work when the cursor is inside a small function? Given the current line, the textobject should be discoverable within 50 lines. Does the message appear for both `iF` and `aF`?

In case the above does not apply, perhaps you can look at how its done in [MiniMax](https://github.com/nvim-mini/MiniMax/blob/ebc8ab181dcfbd0089e00209b5deaa4f32cfb065/configs/nvim-0.12/plugin/40_plugins.lua#L58). Any language added [here](https://github.com/nvim-mini/MiniMax/blob/ebc8ab181dcfbd0089e00209b5deaa4f32cfb065/configs/nvim-0.12/plugin/40_plugins.lua#L53) should work. The suggested config for `mini.ai` can be found [here](https://github.com/nvim-mini/MiniMax/blob/ebc8ab181dcfbd0089e00209b5deaa4f32cfb065/configs/nvim-0.12/plugin/30_mini.lua#L322).

reply_data.body:
On top of this, I'd draw extra attention to making sure that tree-sitter is actually used in specified languages. On the latest 'nvim-treesitter/nvim-treesitter' those are not automatically enabled and require explicit `vim.treesitter.start()` Lua call. I.e. execute `:lua vim.treesitter.start()` and see if it makes textobjects work (or at least highlighting will likely have changed). The links above show the setup that can do this automatically.

The posted config doesn't show it, so my guess would be to first check this.

reply_data.body:
> Maybe warn if the capture is unknown when no match is found to make it more intuitive. As I understand it, the confusion comes from the 50-line message.

This is not the problem here as queries were present from 'nvim-treesitter-textobjects' plugin. The tree-sitter parser was not available and/or enabled for particular buffer. There are errors for completely missing parser (or query), but maybe not in some cases of not enabled parsers.
